title: .NET MAUI 11 Makes CoreCLR the Default Runtime and Adds Incremental XAML Hot Reload
summary:
Microsoft released .NET 11 with a .NET MAUI update focused on product quality. CoreCLR is now the default runtime on all platforms, and XAML gets incremental hot reload, implicit namespaces and faster resource dictionaries. The release also adds device test templates and passkey support, and raises the minimum Android and Apple platform versions.

By Edin Kapić

title: Mock Service Worker Releases v3.0 with ESM-Only Build, Socket-Based Interception and GraphQL Subs
summary:
Mock Service Worker 3.0 is now ESM-only, requires Node.js 22 or later, and cuts package size from 416KB to 234KB. It adds GraphQL subscription support, protocol-specific entrypoints, and an experimental defineNetwork API. Node.js interception now works at the TCP and TLS level. Some users report test failures from newly intercepted OPTIONS preflight requests.

By Daniel Curtis

title: Recap of Microsoft Ignite 2026: Copilot as the Work OS and Agent Governance
summary:
At Ignite 2026, Microsoft positioned Copilot as the operating system for work and extended agent identity, governance, and cost controls across Azure, Foundry, Entra, and Defender. Highlights include Cobalt 200 VMs, Azure HorizonDB, a continuous improvement loop in Foundry, Microsoft IQ, a standalone Azure AI Gateway, and Windows Server 2028.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers

title: GitHub Ditches CSS-in-JS for CSS Modules, Reports 55% Faster SSR After Three-Year Migration
summary:
GitHub migrated github.com from styled-components to CSS Modules over three years, reporting a 55% cut in server-side rendering time and 25% faster component initialisation. Primer components were converted behind feature flags, and about 7,760 sx prop usages were migrated with codemods and Copilot agents. Commenters questioned user impact and hashed class names.

By Daniel Curtis

title: DoorDash Scales Dispatch 10x While Maintaining 99.99% Peak Availability
summary:
DoorDash has redesigned its real-time dispatch platform, replacing a monolithic optimization engine with a distributed architecture that separates coordination from computation. The new system delivers 10x higher throughput and more than 99.99% peak availability. It also supports hybrid machine learning inference and multi-agent reinforcement learning to dynamically optimize delivery assignments.

By Leela Kumili

title: Presentation: Learning Out Loud (Under Near-Existential Pressure)
summary:
Laura Savino discusses the psychological friction of AI adoption for senior engineers & architects. She explains how shifting from static expertise to learning in public lowers anxiety, accelerates tooling fluency, and prevents burnout. Leaders will discover actionable strategies to support their teams, debunk tech zealotry, and foster an adaptive engineering culture that thrives during upheaval.

By Laura Savino

title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts
summary:
Rust 1.100.0, released 12 November 2026, stabilises the never type (!) after ten years of work and makes Infallible an alias for it. The release also stabilises the core of the allocator API, adds DropGuard, and gives Cargo an opt-in dependency cooldown setting. Some critics note the allocator design still lacks inline storage support.

By Daniel Curtis

title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
summary:
AWS has raised the maximum timeout of on-demand Lambda Event Functions from 15 to 30 minutes in all commercial regions, with no opt-in and no new pricing. The limit had stood since 2018. AWS's post lists the costs: twice the concurrency at the same request rate, three-hour SQS visibility timeouts, and Kafka mappings that must be recreated. Practitioners welcome it and ask what belongs elsewhere.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers

title: CNCF Research Shows Virtual Machines Remain Central as AI Workloads Evolve
summary:
New research from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and Linux Foundation Research finds that VMs host an average of 53% of production applications, while emerging AI and agentic workloads are creating additional demand for virtualisation, particularly where stronger execution isolation is required.

By Craig Risi

title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando
summary:
OpenAI has detailed Pando, a new backend that scales Git for concurrent coding-agent workloads without replacing familiar Git workflows. The company reports nearly 80% lower median push latency by coordinating branch updates independently and reusing stored packfiles across fetches.

By Eran Stiller

title: Presentation: Inferencing for Enterprises
summary:
Dio Rettori discusses the operational realities of enterprise AI inference. Moving beyond fast token generation, he explores why inference requires dedicated systems engineering, tackles GPU utilization pitfalls, compares on-prem versus cloud TCO, and analyzes multi-agent latency determinism. He shares why teams must embed domain ontology directly into models rather than relying solely on RAG.

By Dio Rettori

title: Article: Engineering Around Non-Determinism: Evals, Grounding, and Release Gates for AI-Drafted Suspicious Reports
summary:
Moving GenAI into high-stakes production requires treating non-determinism as an engineering problem. This architectural blueprint shows engineering leaders and architects how to build trustworthy agentic workflows using knowledge graphs, dual-layer eval judges, CI/CD release gates, and regression testing against golden datasets to automate drafting while maintaining zero-hallucination compliance.

By Ritesh Modi, Sasidhar Gudala
